project.name: Greeting CLI
project.summary: A tiny local Python command that prints an exact greeting and rejects arguments.

evidence.summary: The command output, exit codes, runtime, and test expectations are explicit.
A single local maintainer is the only actor.
Networked, persistent, deployed, and third-party surfaces are excluded.
The complete greeting journey forms one candidate bounded context and slice.

facts.statement: The application uses Python 3.13 and only its standard library.
The module prints exactly one greeting for an argument-free invocation.

included.statement: Implement and verify the local greeting command and invalid-argument path.

excluded.statement: Browser, API, network, identity, persistence, deployment, and third-party dependencies are excluded.

deferred.statement: CI and remote evidence remain deferred until a remote or multi-contributor surface exists.

actors.statement: One local maintainer invokes and verifies the command.

journeys.statement: The maintainer invokes the module and receives the exact greeting or a concise usage error.

quality_requirements.statement: Automated tests prove exact standard output, standard error, and exit codes.

choices.decision: Use any available Python 3.13 patch and only the standard library.
choices.rationale: The user explicitly selected the runtime line and dependency boundary.

choices.decision: Use unittest and subprocess with unittest discovery as the aggregate gate.
choices.rationale: The verification approach is explicit and adds no external dependency.

capability_assessments.need: Shape the complete greeting journey as an independently verifiable vertical slice.
capability_assessments.semantic_profile: The consumer owns the exact greeting, argument, and console outcome semantics.

capability_assessments.need: Implement and verify a Python 3.13 standard-library command.
capability_assessments.semantic_profile: The consumer owns the Python command implementation semantics.

subdomains.name: Greeting
subdomains.vision: Deliver the exact observable greeting contract for local maintainers.
subdomains.ownership: Owns greeting text, argument policy, exit codes, and console-channel behavior.
subdomains.non_ownership: Does not own web, network, identity, persistence, or deployment concerns.
data_ownership: No durable data; owns invocation inputs and output values in memory.
invariants: An argument-free invocation emits the exact greeting once.
Invalid arguments emit a concise usage error and a non-zero exit code.
subdomains.lifecycle: Changes only with the command's externally observable contract.

candidate_contexts.name: Greeting
candidate_contexts.vision: Own the complete greeting command model and its observable outcomes.
responsibilities: Produce exact standard output, standard error, and exit codes.
non_responsibilities: No network, identity, persistence, deployment, or third-party behavior.
data_ownership: Ephemeral invocation arguments and output result.
invariants: One invocation has one terminal outcome.
candidate_contexts.lifecycle: The context and command contract version together.
candidate_contexts.separation_rationale: One coherent language and consistency boundary covers the entire journey.
split_triggers: Split only if a distinct owner, lifecycle, language, or durable consistency boundary appears.

founding_decision_candidates.title: Keep one greeting model boundary
founding_decision_candidates.question: How many model boundaries does the complete greeting journey require?
founding_decision_candidates.recommended_option: Use one Greeting bounded context with one owned command module.
alternatives: Split valid and invalid invocations into separate contexts.
founding_decision_candidates.rationale: The journey has one language, owner, lifecycle, and consistency boundary.
consequences: Architecture must challenge this candidate and create a Proposed founding ADR.
No network, storage, or deployment boundary is invented.

candidate_slice_signals.statement: The first slice is the complete argument-free and invalid-argument greeting journey.
